title: An Informational Route to Negative Mobility
authors: Ziluo Zhang, Shigeyuki Komura, Zhihong You
abstract: Mobility links an applied force to the resulting motion and is generally positive near equilibrium. Far from equilibrium, however, internal energy input can reverse this response. Here we show that information feedback provides a distinct route to negative mobility. We consider an overdamped dimer consisting of a run-and-tumble particle coupled by a spring to a passive Brownian particle. Information enters through periodic measurements of the relative displacement, which are processed to reset the active polarity. Although the unloaded dimer has no net drift, an applied force biases its internal configuration, and an information-mechanical feedback amplifies and converts this bias into active propulsion against the force, producing negative mobility. We develop an analytical theory that captures this mechanism and yields a feedback-gain criterion for response reversal. Including the information-processing cost reveals a tradeoff: rapid feedback enhances reverse transport but incurs a growing informational cost, yielding an optimal finite feedback rate for information-inclusive efficiency. These results show that information can reshape nonequilibrium response by controlling how internally supplied energy is converted into macroscopic transport.
summary: This paper demonstrates that information feedback can induce negative mobility in a physical dimer system, allowing motion against an applied external force. The authors develop a theory showing that while rapid feedback enhances this reverse transport, it incurs a growing informational cost. Consequently, optimal performance is achieved at a finite, non-zero feedback rate, establishing a fundamental trade-off between control and efficiency.
main_problem: Investigating how information feedback can provide a distinct route to achieving negative mobility (motion opposite to the applied force) in non-equilibrium systems.
main_result: Negative mobility is achieved when the information-mediated active response overcomes the direct mechanical response, and the information-inclusive efficiency shows a trade-off, peaking at a finite feedback rate.
method: Analytical theory development, utilizing stochastic energetics and analyzing the system's dynamics in the overdamped limit.
model_or_system: An overdamped dimer composed of a run-and-tumble particle coupled to a passive Brownian particle. Information is introduced via periodic measurements of the relative displacement to reset the active polarity.
key_observables: Mobility ($\mu$), Mean velocity ($\langle v angle$), Active polarity ($\langle \sigma angle$), Information-inclusive efficiency ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Measurement interval ($	au$), Applied force ($f$), Feedback gain ($\chi\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The system operates in the overdamped limit, and the analysis includes the Landauer bound for information-processing cost.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition to negative mobility in the $(f, 	au)$ plane, and show the trade-off between information cost, active power, and output power.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the basic dynamics and shows the negative mobility regime. It then develops the framework for information-inclusive efficiency, deriving the optimal finite feedback rate that maximizes this efficiency.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, non-equilibrium example of how information processing can fundamentally alter macroscopic transport properties, linking thermodynamics, stochastic dynamics, and information theory.
